assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, the active peptide forms) led to therapies that transformed diabetes and obesity care and now show cardiovascular and renal benefit. The discovery chain is clear, original and of exceptional lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and identification of the active truncated peptide), Drucker (intestinotrophic and receptor biology, translation) and Mojsov (peptide chemistry and identification of the active form) form a plausible trio. Knudsen's industrial medicinal-chemistry role is substantial but a three-person limit forces a choice; Habener and others outside the supplied credit are not available. Priority disputes are unresolved, and my recollection of the details is not independently verified.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent large phase 3 outcome trials and a decade or more of clinical use make the field mature and the recognition timely.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among the peptide-identification, physiology and drug-development contributors is contested.
Exclusion of Knudsen and of researchers not in the credited list may be seen as unfair.
Long-term safety of the class is still accruing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signalling and proteostasis control, with implications for secretory-cell function, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The conceptual novelty and clarity are very high.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently identified the core components (Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing, ATF6 and related signalling). The pair is a natural fit; other contributors such as Ron or Kaufman are not in the credited names, so the prize configuration is cleanly supported by the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: The pathway has been confirmed for over two decades across yeast and mammals, with robust and independent replication, although direct therapeutic translation is still developing.
uncertainties: The pathway is mainly mechanistic, so Nobel impact on medicine rests on downstream disease relevance rather than on an approved therapy.
Omitting other major UPR contributors outside the credited list may be debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells created a new modality of living drugs, producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and now extending to autoimmune disease. Very high clinical impact and originality.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early costimulated CAR design and preclinical work) and June (first clinical successes in leukaemia, 4-1BB CAR construct) are decisive contributors. Rosenberg's pioneering adoptive cell therapy and early CAR trials make him a credible third; Eshhar and others outside the list are not available. Credit is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long-term follow-up confirm efficacy; however toxicity, solid-tumour limits and cost remain, and the field is still evolving, so some may judge it slightly early.
uncertainties: Allocation between CAR design, clinical translation and the wider adoptive-cell tradition is disputed.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, is still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with light, redefining circuit analysis, and has begun to enter clinical vision restoration. A methodological invention of very broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterised channelrhodopsin; Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal use; Miesenboeck made earlier genetically targeted light-control. Six credited names exceed the three-laureate limit and the allocation among discovery of the tool and its neuronal implementation is the main difficulty.
assessment.maturity: The technique is thoroughly confirmed and ubiquitous, although direct medical applications are still at an early stage, so the Physiology or Medicine fit rests on physiology rather than therapy.
uncertainties: Severe credit allocation problem among six candidates.
Medical benefit is still limited, so fit to the prize's medical mandate is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR identification as the central controller of cell growth and nutrient response is a foundational discovery with consequences in cancer, immunosuppression, metabolism and ageing, and led to rapamycin-derived drugs.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered the TOR genes and their role in growth control; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin provided key chemical-biology steps. Sabatini's mTORC1 nutrient-sensing contributions are real but his inclusion is complicated by documented professional conduct concerns, so I would not propose him. Schreiber's role relative to others such as Heitman and Movva is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Highly replicated for three decades; the biology is well-established, while clinical benefits of rapalogs are real but narrower than first hoped.
uncertainties: Contested credit, including Sabatini's conduct issues and the contributions of the original rapamycin discoverers.
Clinical impact of mTOR inhibitors is narrower than the basic-science impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of tau and alpha-synuclein as the principal components of neuropathological filaments in Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and related diseases reshaped the molecular classification of neurodegeneration and underpins current biomarker and seed-amplification assays and trials.
assessment.attribution: Goedert and Spillantini are the clear central figures on the supplied credit, and the pair is a coherent two-person configuration. As a neurologist I note the field's other pioneers outside the list, and I do not treat my own research interests as a reason to favour this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Findings are over 25 years old and confirmed by cryo-EM structural work and clinical biomarkers, though disease-modifying therapies are not yet established.
uncertainties: No approved therapy yet derives directly from this work.
Relative importance versus the amyloid and other competing neurodegeneration frameworks is debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition provided the first convincing proof of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, converting chronic myeloid leukaemia into a manageable chronic disease. Outstanding clinical and conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) are a natural trio. Others, such as Rowley and Witte for the underlying genetics, were part of an earlier chain and are not on the credited list.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of clinical use with survival data; mature, and recognition is arguably overdue, although earlier Lasker recognition suggests the field has long been regarded as Nobel-class.
uncertainties: Priority relating to the earlier cytogenetic and oncogene discoveries is not credited here.
Industrial versus academic credit allocation may be contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF blockade treats rheumatoid arthritis established cytokine targeting as a therapeutic principle and transformed outcomes across several inflammatory diseases.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini made the decisive translational demonstration of anti-TNF efficacy, a clear two-person configuration. Other contributors to TNF biology and antibody engineering are not on the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Extensively replicated, with a large clinical record and biosimilars; very mature and timely if not overdue.
uncertainties: Discovery of TNF itself and of the antibodies is not credited to these two.
Therapeutic rather than mechanistic emphasis may weigh against the candidate.
